mcat_description.short: Portable Buildings are prefabricated, relocatable structures — primarily steel-framed porta cabins, container offices, and modular site cabins — manufactured off-site and assembled on-site for temporary or semi-permanent use. They are sold as complete units or on a per-square-foot basis, customised to buyer specifications.
mcat_description.long: Portable Buildings encompass factory-manufactured, relocatable structures built using structural steel frames and insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rockwool core), designed for rapid deployment and easy relocation across project sites. The category spans a wide range of functional types — from compact security guard cabins and portable site offices to multi-room labour colonies, portable classrooms, portable shops, and container-converted accommodation units. In the Indian market, these structures are governed by IS 15917:2010 (BIS standard for prefabricated construction) and the National Building Code 2016, with materials including MS steel, GI, PVC, and cement board. Buyers range from construction contractors and industrial facility managers to institutional bodies and event operators, all seeking fast-deployment, cost-effective alternatives to permanent RCC construction.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Portable Buildings' is commercially synonymous with 'porta cabins' and 'prefab cabins' — steel-framed, insulated, factory-manufactured structures deployed for temporary or semi-permanent use. The dominant construction method uses MS/GI steel structural frames combined with PUF (polyurethane foam) or EPS sandwich panels, with aluminium windows and steel flooring. The governing Indian standard is IS 15917:2010 (BIS — Building Design and Erection Using Prefabricated Construction), and structures must comply with the National Building Code of India 2016. India's prefabricated building market was valued at USD 14–15 billion in 2023–24 (single source — re-thinkingthefuture.com, low confidence on exact figure) and is growing at above 10% annually, with modular container housing growing at 13.5% CAGR. Key buyer segments are construction contractors, industrial facility managers, and institutional buyers (schools, hospitals, government). The trade term 'Kota Cabin' is a widely used regional synonym for porta cabin in buyer vocabulary. Sellers are concentrated in Hyderabad, Pune, Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, and Vadodara. The product is sold on a per-sq-ft basis for custom structures and per-piece for standard compact units.
